findings.reasoning: The `init` function is public and has no authorization checks, allowing any external account to modify the `map` mapping arbitrarily, including triggering the underflow described above.

The statement `map[k] -= v;` performs subtraction on a uint256 without any checks. In Solidity 0.4.11 arithmetic is unchecked, so if `v` is greater than the current value stored at `map[k]`, the value will underflow and wrap around to a very large number, which can be abused to manipulate the mapping state.
